newsitem.title: USA: Mid-West spot power seen mostly higher through Mon.
newsitem.headline: Mid-West spot power seen mostly higher through Mon.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West were mostly higher Friday for Monday business with cold weather expected to dominate through to at least the end of November, sources said.
Short-term deals were said to be fairly scarce however, with many traders looking to do December or weekly business in light of the Thanksgiving Holiday next week.
IES Utilities Inc's 538 megawatt Duane Arnold nuclear power plant in Palo, Iowa was likely to reach full output over the weekend after a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage.
The 440 megawatt Big Stone coal-fired power plant in Big Stone City, S.D., will likely return to full service on Sunday after scheduled maintenance, Northwestern Public Service said.
Minnkota Power Coopertive said the 439 megawatt Milton Young coal-fired power unit 2 in Center, N.D., was likely to return to service early Saturday following boiler repairs.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm next day power deals were pegged slightly higher for Monday business at $27.50-29.50 from next-day discussion at $27.00-29.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Thursday, the brokers and marketers said.
Weekend peak MAPP power was assessed in the $15.50-18.50 range, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power prices were said to have eased to $12.00-14.00 through the weekend from discussion at $14.00-16.00 on Thursday.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm power for Monday delivery was pegged higher at $25.00-27.00 from $23.00-25.00 in Thursday discussion.
Weekend peak MAIN power was assessed at $15.50-17.50 per MWh, the sources said.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Monday delivery were notionally assessed at $27.00-29.00 from next-day talk at $20.00-21.50 on Thursday.
Monday deals for ECAR were said to be elusive, with most players looking to seal business for all of next week, where unconfirmed deals said to have been done at $24.00 per MWh.
Weekend ECAR power was notionally assessed in the $15.00-18.50 range, the sources said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power for Monday was notionally assessed lower at $13.00-15.00 from $15.00-17.00 on Thursday.
December peak ECAR was talked steady at $22.00-23.00, with January/February ECAR also assessed steady at $23.00-24.00 per MWh.
Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) for the weekend and Monday were talked steady to higher at $25.00-27.50 from $25.00-26.00 in Thursday discussion.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were notionally said to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area, traders said.
December SPP was assessed steady at $26.50-27.50, the brokers and marketers said.
--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627
